simulator.tau_markerlight_all_detach.quoted_text: Each time a T'AU EMPIRE unit from your army (excluding KROOT units) is selected to shoot, ranged weapons equipped by models in your unit have their Ballistic Skill characteristic improved by 1 and have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units that are not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy models.
simulator.tau_markerlight_all_detach.trigger: any T'au Empire (non-KROOT) detachment is shooting in the simulator's batched Shooting window — gated by env var SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_ALL_DETACH=1 (default OFF). The base sim only ran Battle._run_markerlight_phase for detachments carrying the Mont'ka-only `lethal_hits_on_guided` flag (an early-exit at code/simulator.py), so non-Mont'ka T'au (e.g. Kauyon) received ZERO Guided uptime even though the consumer in code/units.py reads `guided_enemy_uids` without checking that flag.
simulator.tau_markerlight_all_detach.effect: GATE 1 (SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_ALL_DETACH, default OFF, byte-identical when unset): when ON, the base Markerlight phase runs for ALL T'au detachments (the `lethal_hits_on_guided` early-exit is bypassed; the phase still returns when there is no resolved detachment). This restores the army-wide base Guided buff (+1 to the Hit roll and [SUSTAINED HITS 1] vs the marked target) for every T'au detachment and every round, as the rule is army-wide. The Mont'ka-specific Lethal-Hits-on-Guided remains gated on the `lethal_hits_on_guided` flag in Unit.attack and is unchanged by this gate. APPROXIMATION: marking still follows the existing per-carrier model (one carrier marks the highest-points enemy in 36" + line of sight per the per-shot emission rule `simulator.markerlight_emission`); this gate only changes WHICH detachments the phase runs for, not how a single carrier marks.

simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.rule_name: Markerlights / Guided (line-of-sight condition, not a per-attacker hit roll)
simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.quoted_text: Each time a T'AU EMPIRE unit from your army (excluding KROOT units) is selected to shoot, ranged weapons equipped by models in your unit have their Ballistic Skill characteristic improved by 1 and have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units that are not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy models.
simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.trigger: a T'au Empire (non-KROOT) unit shoots an enemy unit that is visible (line of sight) to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units — gated by env var SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_BASE_LOS=1 (default OFF). The verbatim rule grants the buff on the line-of-sight / markerlight-token condition ("while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units"), NOT on a per-attacker Ballistic-Skill hit roll. The base sim instead gates the buff on `Army.guided_enemy_uids`, which is populated only when a per-carrier d6 to-hit roll succeeds inside Battle._run_markerlight_phase — firing the base buff only about half the time the real rule should.
simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.effect: GATE 2 (SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_BASE_LOS, default OFF, byte-identical when unset): when ON, Battle._run_markerlight_phase additionally builds `Army.guided_los_enemy_uids` — every alive enemy unit within 36" + line of sight + a legal target (Look Out Sir / Lone Operative) of AT LEAST ONE friendly MARKERLIGHT carrier, with NO per-carrier to-hit roll — and the base Guided buff branches in Unit.attack (the +1-to-Hit hit-modifier branch and the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] sustained-hits branch) read this line-of-sight set instead of `guided_enemy_uids`. The Mont'ka [LETHAL HITS] consumer keeps reading the hit-roll-gated `guided_enemy_uids`, so only the BASE buff's gating changes. When OFF, `guided_los_enemy_uids` is never populated or read and the base buff continues to read `guided_enemy_uids` exactly as before. APPROXIMATION: the simulator has no physical Markerlight token object, so visibility-to-a-MARKERLIGHT-unit is modelled as the carrier's own line of sight + 36" range + target eligibility (the same geometry the per-shot emission gate uses), which is the most defensible faithful reading of "visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units".
